evals.prompt: Define autonomous loop patterns for AI agent systems in 2-3 sentences.
evals.expected_output: They are reusable control shapes for running an agent repeatedly until an explicit stop condition, safety cap, or human handoff is reached. A correct definition mentions progress signals, durable state, stop conditions, and caps.
expectations: Defines loops as control shapes, not just repeated prompting
Mentions stop condition, progress evidence, durable state, and safety cap
Does NOT define autonomy as permission to run indefinitely

evals.prompt: Name the primitives in the mental model for autonomous loop patterns and explain how they fit together.
evals.expected_output: The primitives are trigger, worker agent, progress signal, stop condition, durable state, and safety cap. A trigger starts an iteration, the worker acts, progress evidence is recorded, durable state preserves resume context, the stop condition ends the loop, and the cap prevents unsafe continuation.
expectations: Names at least five of the six primitives
Explains the relationships between primitives, not just a list
Does NOT omit the safety cap or durable state primitives

evals.prompt: Why should an agent team use named loop patterns instead of ad hoc continue instructions?
evals.expected_output: Named loop patterns make termination, recovery, state persistence, and escalation explicit. They prevent uncapped retry, lost progress after restart, and silent stalls that ad hoc continue instructions cannot reliably handle.
expectations: Explains the failure modes named patterns prevent
Connects the purpose to safety and recoverability
Does NOT claim prompt wording alone is enough for reliable loop control

evals.prompt: Explain how autonomous-loop-patterns differs from prompt-craft, tool-call-strategy, agent-engineering, context-management, and observability-modeling.
evals.expected_output: Autonomous-loop-patterns owns repeated-execution control shape. Prompt-craft owns one worker instruction, tool-call-strategy owns per-tool efficiency, agent-engineering owns the broader system architecture, context-management owns what enters one worker context, and observability-modeling owns telemetry semantics.
expectations: Routes each adjacent concept to the right neighboring skill
Keeps autonomous-loop-patterns focused on loop control shape
Does NOT let autonomous-loop-patterns over-own prompt writing, tool optimization, or telemetry schema design

evals.prompt: Classify bounded single-run, sentinel continuation, checkpoint-resume, supervisor respawn, and human-gated loops by best use case.
evals.expected_output: Bounded single-run fits one clear task; sentinel continuation fits small repeated turns with a precise marker; checkpoint-resume fits multi-session work; supervisor respawn fits many independent queue items; human-gated loops fit risky or unclear work.
expectations: Maps each pattern to a distinct use case
Recognizes human-gated loops as a safety pattern
Does NOT treat supervisor respawn as the default for every task

evals.prompt: Use the autopilot analogy for autonomous loop patterns and map it to concrete loop primitives.
evals.expected_output: The worker agent is the aircraft, progress signals are instruments, durable state is the flight log, safety caps are altitude or fuel limits, stop conditions are route completion or abort rules, and human handoff is the pilot taking control.
expectations: Preserves the control-system structure of the analogy
Maps at least four concrete loop primitives
Does NOT imply autopilot removes the need for human handoff or safety limits

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: an agent should review a small batch of five independent markdown files overnight, creating a short report for each. Choose a loop pattern and list required safety mechanisms.
evals.expected_output: A supervisor respawn loop is reasonable if each file is independent and fresh context per file matters; otherwise a bounded or checkpoint loop may be enough. Required safeguards include per-item status, timeout, consecutive-error cap, durable report path, and visible stop reason.
expectations: Chooses a pattern based on independence and context needs
Includes durable status and safety caps
Explains when a simpler pattern would be enough
Does NOT approve an unattended loop without timeout or error cap
